system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Price-sensitive SMB 40% off: signups +31%, rev +18%, retention -12%. Measured over four weeks in the standard SMB segment.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale:
The presenting symptoms are activation -6% and onboarding completion -4%, which points at the funnel itself rather than at price. The obvious competitive reflex is promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is the one inherited record with a clean quantified downside: 40% off bought +31% signups and +18% revenue while costing 12% retention over only four weeks. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that trade is negative-to-neutral at best, and matching a competitor's entry price also anchors the segment we most want to keep. So I am not spending the single slot there.

I intend simplify_onboarding. It attacks both declining metrics at their shared upstream point, and two inherited memories (memory_31 SMB activation lift, memory_86 completion and time-to-value lift) point the same way. That convergence is exactly why I want the verification budget spent on those two rather than on the pricing record, whose weakness is already explicit. My concern is that memory_31 and memory_86 may not be independent evidence: consolidated 28 days apart, describing overlapping mechanisms on overlapping populations, they could be two summaries of one underlying experiment or a re-measurement of the same cohort. If so my apparent double confirmation collapses to a single data point and I should size down accordingly. I want the archived records to tell me the segment, the sample, whether the lift was measured beyond first-week activation, and whether the effect persisted or decayed.

Downstream value risk: memory_44 says enterprise converts better through sales-assisted demo-request flows. Cutting required signup fields is precisely the mechanism that could strip the qualification signal used to route enterprise prospects into that path, trading a visible SMB activation gain for an invisible loss of high-quality pipeline. That harm would not surface in the activation metric the experiment is scored on. So I scope the test to the self-serve SMB segment, leave the demo-request path untouched, and instrument demo-request rate and downstream pipeline quality as explicit guardrails alongside the headline activation number.

Uncertainty I am carrying forward rather than resolving: all six memories are compressed summaries with archived sources, none carry confidence intervals, and none were measured against the current competitive environment, in which SMB behavior may simply differ from day 12 or day 52. A lift that was durable pre-competitor is not guaranteed durable now. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the fallback if verification shows the onboarding memories are a single weak or decayed result; referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address the funnel decline, so it is wrong for this week regardless.
